> I am unsure why this is not already a feature, but it really should be.

You've listed a list, not a single feature, so that is why it's not already a feature I suppose. 

For the BIO and status I think it's important to consider that any account on vrchat can see your BIO and status. I can see if you're on orange, won't be able to see if you're actually on vrchat or not. If you block the display of a BIO towards an account that you've blocked, you now guarantee that anyone can easily check if you're blocking them.

For mutual friends, I wonder if vrchat has considered an option to make mutual friends a friend only. But like I don't think I see the issue there, some people on vrchat will accept any friend request, and some are choosey. In my experience of having to block someone in a friend group, who knows who isn't really a mystery. 

But yeah for mutuals it should be visible to everyone, friends, or nobody.

details:
For safety reasons, Discord has implemented similar systems I want to propose, this is an idea that is out of necessity. Safety of others on this platform and should *always* be a priority. Blocking should be more meaningful on a SOCIAL platform. I've long been aware of malicious actors knowing too much about you at a glance and with tools like VRCX, you should be protected from such people to the extent that this platform can allow.

With rewriting the Blocking System, you'll inhibit their ability to know about you better:

They are unable to see your mutual friends. This makes it harder for them to reach you through your own friend networks.

They are unable to see your bio. It reads as the default bio text for a new account.

They are unable to see your status. It will be set to "Do Not Disturb" or "OFFLINE"

They are unable to see your Groups (and mutual groups). It will show you're not even a member. 

(bypassed by administrator/moderator roles if you have them)

You receive tooltips informing you a blocked user has joined your instance to keep you informed.

I am unsure why this is not already a feature, but it really should be.
title: Blocking Isn't Helpful Enough
